1.why: Only option describing a two-sided critique plus a new criterion; the others commit to one side, which SAT structure keys rarely do.

2.why: Most hedged structural description (rival accounts, opposite predictions, obstacle to testing); the others assert a resolution.

3.why: 'Retrospective compilations' is the precise, non-contemporaneous option that a 'most logical and precise' blank usually rewards.

4.why: Kahneman-style point: subjective confidence is equal across valid and invalid environments. Others are absolute or blame training.

5.why: Standard paired-text move: deflating a cognitive-understanding claim with associative/reward learning rather than denying the behavior.

6.why: Matches the well-known microcredit RCT result: business activity up, poverty/well-being unchanged; the others overclaim.

7.why: 'Insufficient on their own' is the hedged inference; B and D are absolutes, A takes a side.

8.why: A, B, C all use absolutes ('only', 'permanently', 'inevitable'); D is the moderate conditional inference.

9.why: Text 2 typically adds a regime-shift objection; 'insufficient' is the standard counter to a catch-limit remedy.

10.why: Function question about a closing pivot sentence quoting 'doing the judging' — relocating the defect to the evaluative framework.

11.why: Concede-and-extend response; the others change the subject to enforcement or survey frequency.

12.why: A 'function in the text as a whole' key usually names the sentence's role in setting up the passage's doubt, not its content.

13.why: The quoted sentence justifies proportion, so it explains why so much space went to a failure.

14.why: Attacks the aggregate-to-local inference behind 'proportionate declines'; the others quibble with magnitude or cost.

15.why: Vocabulary items key the figurative sense, not the literal pigment senses.

16.why: Only finding that varies bystander presence while holding the client constant — a direct audience-effect test.

17.why: Fire-suppression critique: serotinous cones plus fuel buildup and more severe fires.

18.why: Revisionist claims about non-natives are usually conditional on degraded systems; C is the specific supporting case, D is too sweeping.

19.why: Cost-of-overland-transport evidence is the load-bearing economic support; the others are incidental.

20.why: 'Economy' of an artwork means spareness; frugality is the money-sense near-miss.

21.why: 'Predictable' is the analytic term such blanks usually want over the more concrete alternatives.

22.why: Timing evidence (rise before schooling campaigns) directly supports a causal print claim; B is the counter-finding.

23.why: Difference questions key an accurate, hedged summary of Text 2; B, C, D are overstatements or denials of settled data.

24.why: Closing-sentence function is usually to generalize from the instance just described.
